olivia: Heads-up: we have a planned L7 payload rollout across eu1 and eu2 tonight (compliance sample). Before we flip, saw a simulation that shows potential KMS grant amplification when payloads go direct. Splitting the plan here.
samir: Good catch. What did the simulation show?
olivia: Ran a 10k-event batch against the audit pipeline in staging using direct-to-S3 mode. Each event caused a keystore decrypt call -> total decrypts ~= 10k. With aggregator path we simulated batching and saw decrypts ~= 120 (per-batch).
kevin: That's ~83x amplification. If that reproduces in prod we'll exhaust KMS grants in seconds when multiple nodes join.
sre_lead: We need an automated preflight gate. Proposal: before any rollout, run a short, low-volume canary that enables payloads with sampling 1% and measure keystore.decrypt.rate. If it exceeds threshold abort.
security_jen: Compliance will push back on sampling for the sample, but we can document the safety window. Also propose a parallel design: route L7 payloads via the fw-aggregator service which performs one decrypt per batch and forwards a single record.
samir: Architect note: the aggregator can call the keystore once per batch if it holds the encrypted material and re-attaches plaintext to the batch. That avoids per-event decrypts from every node. But aggregator must be trusted and we need HSM/KMS grant permissions for that service principal.
kevin: Ops note: aggregator adds a network hop and minor latency; acceptable for audit. But we still need a fallback if aggregator OOMs or S3 upstream is slow.
olivia: Action items I suggest: 1) Add a canary workflow with sampling and a preflight KMS-sim check (simulate joins with test keys) 2) Implement aggregator route and test it end-to-end in eu1 staging 3) Add metric alarm: keystore.decrypt/s >= 100 -> rollback firewall policy 4) File KMS grant QPS increase request for keystore service as contingency.
sre_lead: +1. Also add a safety lambda that watches keystore.decrypt/error_rate > 2% for 90s and flips fw audit.l7_payload=false for the region automatically. Lambda must annotate incidents and avoid flipping during planned experiments (a lock).
security_jen: I'll prepare a compliance exception template for the canary and the fallback policy wording. We need to state how long richer logs will be withheld and when aggregator rollout is expected.
samir: Small implementation detail: aggregator must batch by tenant/workload window to avoid cross-tenant mixing. We'll include tenant-id in batch boundary and add strict auth.
kevin: Cost forecast: aggregator adds EC2 cost but reduces KMS decrypts drastically. Rough estimate: aggregator infra ~+$1200/month across EU, while direct mode could add ~$8k/mo in KMS/S3 for expected volume. I'll produce a quick TCO.
olivia: Runbook updates: if nodes fail to decrypt during onboarding, run keystore/debug-onboard which includes: check keystore service logs -> confirm KMS ThrottlingException -> flip firewall payload off -> drain and retry nodes. We should also include a postmortem checklist and cost calc.
sre_lead: Who owns what? olivia: implement canary + runbook update. samir: aggregator design + security review. kevin: cost TCO & KMS request. security_jen: compliance doc + exception. I'll own the lambda rollback and alarm wiring.
ops-bot: Created incident placeholder: incident/1781234567 - "Planned L7 payload rollout: preflight & safety controls". Runbook linked.
kevin: One more ask 12: can we get a temporary keystore grant cache on nodes (in-memory TTL 30s) so repeated decrypts during bootstrap are deduped? That would be low-effort and help.
samir: That could help but needs cryptographic review. The cache must evict on key rotation and not persist to disk. I'll prototype a node-side cache in staging.
olivia: Nice. Timeline: start canary tonight at 23:00 UTC with sampling 1% for eu1, e2; monitor for 30m. If clear, enable aggregator path and announce 48h guarded rollout.
security_jen: I'll sync with compliance and post the exception before 22:00 UTC.
sre_lead: Good. Post status updates to this thread when canary starts and ends. Keep alerts loud.
olivia: Thanks team. We'll keep payload off in other regions until aggregator is validated.
ops-bot: Canary scheduled: 2026-03-23T23:00:00Z. Will post runbook progress and metrics.
